administration.cycle_and_sequence: Six 21-day cycles before surgery: Phesgo and carboplatin on Day 1; paclitaxel on Days 1 and 8. There is no planned Day 15 paclitaxel. Surgery and pathology determine postoperative HER2 therapy.
route_and_duration: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Complete the observation before chemotherapy. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin.
practical_workflow: Confirm blood results, cardiac checks, active phase, previous dual HER2 dose and the consent discussion.

After Phesgo observation, chemotherapy is given through a cannula, PICC or port. The team explains access insertion and care. No take-home infusion pump is routinely used.
Confirm supportive medicines, next visits and due tests. Injection time is shorter than the whole appointment; preparation, assessment and observation still take time.
observation_and_access: The team checks the last dual HER2 dose, including IV treatment: a gap of less than 6 weeks uses the maintenance dose; 6 weeks or longer needs reloading. A first Phesgo visit after IV treatment does not automatically require a loading dose.

The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

treatment_rationale.summary: Uses an anthracycline-free paclitaxel/carboplatin backbone with dual HER2 blockade before surgery. TRAIN-2 supports the anthracycline-omission strategy, while the NCCP six-cycle schedule is not identical to the original trial schedule.
treatment_rationale.setting: Neoadjuvant locally advanced, inflammatory or high-risk early HER2-positive breast cancer
treatment_rationale.line: Preoperative treatment; NCCP 00790 specifies six 21-day cycles, then surgery and pathology-directed adjuvant review
factors: Confirm disease risk, cardiac function, marrow reserve, renal assessment and neuropathy risk.
Day 1 and day 8 chemotherapy visits differ from three-weekly docetaxel TCHP.
Explain that clinical response and surgical pathology guide the subsequent systemic, radiation and endocrine phases.
alternatives: Choose the taxane/platinum backbone using disease risk, comorbidity, neuropathy, marrow reserve and treatment burden. TRYPHAENA and TRAIN-2 are different studies; cross-trial response percentages cannot rank their regimens.

DESTINY-Breast11 reports newer neoadjuvant pCR evidence for trastuzumab deruxtecan followed by THP versus ddAC followed by THP. It did not directly compare against this NCCP regimen; survival results were immature in that report.

Reassess after surgery. Residual invasive disease can change the postoperative strategy: KATHERINE supports T-DM1 over trastuzumab, while DESTINY-Breast05 provides newer T-DXd versus T-DM1 evidence in a selected high-risk residual-disease population, with additional lung toxicity considerations. These decisions are separate from this neoadjuvant card.
treatment_rationale.limitations: Alternatives require current NCCP, local access and individual MDT review; trial publication alone does not establish Irish availability or authorize a change to this regimen.

evidence_at_a_glance.trial: TRAIN-2 phase III — original IV-antibody strategy; FeDeriCa route bridge
evidence_at_a_glance.population: 438 patients with stage II–III HER2-positive breast cancer
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: Nine paclitaxel/carboplatin cycles without anthracyclines versus three FEC then six paclitaxel/carboplatin cycles; both used IV trastuzumab/pertuzumab.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Important schedule difference: NCCP 00790 prescribes six cycles; the trial non-anthracycline arm used nine. These outcomes support the strategy but are not direct efficacy estimates for six-cycle Phesgo/00790.

endpoints.definition: ypT0/is ypN0: no invasive tumour in breast or axillary nodes; breast in-situ disease permitted.
endpoints.interpretation: Similar observed response; no demonstrated pCR advantage from anthracyclines (P=0.95).
endpoints.limitations: 140/206 without anthracyclines (95% CI 61–74%) and 141/212 with anthracyclines (95% CI 60–73%). This is not proof of survival equivalence or of the NCCP shorter schedule.

endpoints.definition: From randomization to progression causing inoperability, recurrence, secondary primary malignancy or death; contralateral DCIS excluded.
endpoints.interpretation: No demonstrated EFS difference; the study was not powered to establish survival equivalence.
endpoints.limitations: Wide uncertainty. Original trial duration, IV administration and postoperative treatment differ from current pathway decisions.

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: FeDeriCa supports subcutaneous administration through pharmacokinetic non-inferiority in early breast cancer; it does not establish an additional survival benefit from changing the administration route.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Anthracycline-containing treatment produced more febrile neutropenia and cardiac toxicity in TRAIN-2. The anthracycline-free arm still had substantial marrow suppression, diarrhoea and neuropathy.
limitations: The six-versus-nine-cycle discrepancy is retained visibly above the outcome cards; no numerical benefit is claimed for shortening treatment.
pCR is a pathological response endpoint, not proof of cure. Survival analyses were descriptive and underpowered.
The original trial predated routine postoperative T-DM1 for residual disease. KATHERINE, DESTINY-Breast05 and newer neoadjuvant DESTINY-Breast11 evidence require separate eligibility and MDT review.
